bibl.title: Studies in the Reception of Pindar in Ptolemaic Poetry
bibl.seg: Alexandros Kampakoglou, Studies in the Reception of Pindar in Ptolemaic Poetry = Trends in Classics. Supplementary Volumes. 76.
Berlin - Boston, W. de Gruyter, 2019, xiv-454 pp. ISBN 978-3-11-064140-0. €129,95.

C.R. par Susan A. Stephens, BMCRev < https://bmcr.brynmawr.edu/2020/2020.04.21 >. - Antje Kolde, Aitia 10 (2020) < https://journals-openedition-org.scd-rproxy.u-strasbg.fr/aitia/8536 >. - Orlando Poltera, Gnomon 93 (2021) pp. 297-301.
bibl.note: Introduction: reception as a cultural phenomenon and textual process. - Part I: Epinician poetry and discourse: 1. Performing praise in Ptolemaic Alexandria: Callimachus's epinician elegies; - 2. The reception of Pindar in Posidippus's Hippika (AB 71–88); - 3. Epinician echoes in Apollonius's Argonautica: heroic foils and the poetics of immortality. - Part II: Encomia and Hymns: 4. Pindaric eschatology and inherent excellence in Theocritus's Idyll 17; - 5. The mytho-poetics of praise: prodigious Heracles in Pindar and Theocritus 24; - 6. Pindaric theogonies and the poetics of Callimachus's Hymn to Zeus; - 7. Textualizing Cyrenean choreia in Callimachus's Hymn to Apollo; - 8. Defining the elusive: tradition and innovation in Callimachus's Hymn to Delos. - Part III: Myth and Poetry: 9. The poetics of experimentation: generic hybridization and the Argonautic myth. - Afterword. - Works cited. Index of Greek words. Index of passages discussed. Index of subjects.
